original_question: Let G = (V, E, omega) be a weighted simple graph, let W = V be the witness set, and let L subseteq V be an epsilon-net used to build the filtered Dowker complex Dow_alpha(W, L). Determine how to choose epsilon and how to select the epsilon-net L so that, for sufficiently large alpha, the one-dimensional persistence diagram PD_1(Dow_alpha(W, L)) has as many points as the genus of G. Assuming such an epsilon-net is given, bound the bottleneck distance between PD_1(VR_alpha(G)) and PD_1(Dow_alpha(W, L)) in terms of the cycle lengths of G and epsilon.
target_in_paper: Section 1, Open Problem 1.3 in The Dowker complex in metric graphs
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target. It correctly identifies the graph-theoretic setting G = (V, E, omega), fixes the witness set as W = V, uses an epsilon-net L of vertices, asks for conditions ensuring that the one-dimensional Dowker persistence captures the genus of G, and then asks for a bottleneck-distance comparison with the one-dimensional Vietoris-Rips persistence in terms of epsilon and cycle lengths. This is essentially the content of Open Problem 1.3.
missing_details: The paper's background implicitly uses the geodesic metric d_G induced by a connected weighted simple graph; connectedness and the finiteness of d_G on V are hidden assumptions that are not stated in the draft.

The paper defines an epsilon-net in the metric space (V, d_G) as a set L that is both an epsilon-sample and epsilon-sparse: every vertex of V lies within distance epsilon of some landmark in L, and any two distinct landmarks are more than epsilon apart.

To make the question fully stand-alone, the filtered objects should be named explicitly as the filtrations {Dow_alpha(W, L)}_{alpha >= 0} and {VR_alpha(G)}_{alpha >= 0}; otherwise the notation PD_1(Dow_alpha(W, L)) is not standard, since a persistence diagram is attached to a filtration, not to a single complex at one scale.
The paper defines Dow_alpha(W, L) using the geodesic metric: a simplex sigma subseteq L belongs to Dow_alpha(W, L) if there exists w in W such that d_G(w, l) <= alpha for every l in sigma.
The genus of G is not just an informal cycle count; in the nearby context it is specified as the cardinality of a minimal system of cycles of G.
The paper's persistence-diagram notation counts points with multiplicity and only off-diagonal points, so cardinality should be understood in that sense.
The term d_B should be stated explicitly as the bottleneck distance between persistence diagrams.
Cycle lengths should be understood as weighted lengths coming from omega, i.e. sums of edge weights along cycles, not merely combinatorial cycle lengths.
For a fully self-contained mathematical statement, one should fix homology coefficients over a field; the paper leaves coefficients implicit.

The phrase for sufficiently large alpha is not formalized in the draft and is slightly ambiguous in the paper as written, so a sharpened stand-alone version should recast the statement in terms of the whole filtered Dowker and Vietoris-Rips constructions.
refined_question: Fix a field k for persistent homology coefficients. Let G = (V, E, omega) be a connected weighted simple graph with positive edge weights, let d_G be the geodesic metric on V, let W = V, and let L subseteq V be an epsilon-net in (V, d_G), meaning that every v in V satisfies d_G(v, L) <= epsilon and every distinct l, l' in L satisfy d_G(l, l') > epsilon. For the filtered Dowker complex {Dow_alpha(W, L)}_{alpha >= 0}, where a simplex sigma subseteq L lies in Dow_alpha(W, L) iff there exists w in W with d_G(w, l) <= alpha for all l in sigma, determine epsilon > 0 and a rule for choosing the epsilon-net L so that the one-dimensional persistence diagram PD_1({Dow_alpha(W, L)}_{alpha >= 0}) has exactly genus(G) off-diagonal points counted with multiplicity, where genus(G) is the cardinality of a minimal system of cycles of G. Assuming such an epsilon-net L has been chosen, find a bound for the bottleneck distance d_B between PD_1({VR_alpha(G)}_{alpha >= 0}) and PD_1({Dow_alpha(W, L)}_{alpha >= 0}), where VR_alpha(G) is the Vietoris-Rips complex on (V, d_G), in terms of epsilon and the weighted lengths of cycles in G.
justification: The draft is aiming at Open Problem 1.3, not at a neighboring problem. The paper first sets up the metric-graph framework and persistent-homology notation, then defines Vietoris-Rips complexes, Dowker complexes, and epsilon-nets in exactly the form used by your draft. The motivating paragraph immediately before Open Problem 1.3 states that, for metric graphs, the one-dimensional Vietoris-Rips persistence diagram has as many points as the genus of G for large enough scale, and Open Problem 1.3 then asks precisely for: (i) a choice of epsilon and an epsilon-net L with W = V so that the Dowker persistence diagram has the same genus-sized cardinality, and (ii) a bottleneck-distance bound between the one-dimensional Vietoris-Rips and Dowker persistence diagrams in terms of cycle lengths and epsilon. The main sharpening needed is to make the filtration-level notation and the hidden metric assumptions explicit.
